we have identified a novel variant in the PIH1 gene, which is associated with primary ciliary disease.
a c.355 C>T variant of the gene PIH1D was identified in a Chinese pedigree with PCD.
a novel variant in the PIH1 domain of PIH1 D3 gene was identified as the cause for PCD in the pedigree, and the PIH1 D 3 gene is a new PCD gene.

a novel variant of PIHID3, and it is the first report of a PIH1D variant in PCD in the world.
the first report of PIH1 domain variant of PIHID3 gene in a pedigree affected with PCD in China.
the genotype-phenotype relationship of PCD, which will help in understanding the molecular mechanisms of PCD.

PIH1D is a new gene that causes PCD.
the PIH1 variant in the PIH1 domain of the PIHID3 gene is the pathogenic variant for the Chinese pedigree affected with PCD.
the c.355C > T mutation in the PIH1 domain of the PIHID3 gene is associated with PCD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a new PCD-causing variant in a Chinese family and provided a new evidence for the pathogenicity of this gene.
a c.355 C>T variant of PIHID3 gene is a pathogenic variant of PCD.
the c.355C > T variant of PIHID3 can cause primary ciliary dyskinetic disease in Chinese population.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PIH1D1 is essential for the assembly of dynein arms, which is important for the normal beating of cilia and the normal swimming of sperm.
the PIH1 domain is essential for the normal structure and function of cilia and the sperm flagella.
